brief: Zero Hedge relays Hugh Hendry's argument, published as 30-year Treasury yields near 5.50% and this week's 2Y/5Y/7Y auctions showed large tails. Hendry argues the gold standard is dead but its deflationary arithmetic is not: Kindleberger's insight was that the 1930s world lost its stabiliser when Britain, hollowed out as a creditor by WWI, returned sterling to gold in 1925 at the old $4.86 parity, overvaluing the currency and forcing the Bank of England to raise rates and deflate the domestic economy, while the new creditors, America and France, sterilised rather than expanded credit against the gold inflow, breaking the standard's supposed symmetry. Applied to 2026: surplus savers like China are recycling less into US duration at the old yield just as fiscal deficits and an AI buildout both compete for capital, so the clearing yield on Treasuries must rise, rationing mortgages, private credit, equity multiples and the AI buildout itself. He rejects "China stops buying Treasuries and America goes broke" since the US cannot involuntarily run out of its own currency; the constraint instead falls on inflation, the dollar, political legitimacy, and duration's price. His trade: short duration, sized as a medium-term trade rather than a permanent short on America.
